newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profit-taking lowers Stantronic at debut.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking lowers Stantronic at debut.

text.p: Shares in electronics firm Stantronic Group Holdings had a mixed debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday as some investors, who picked up stock in the group's private stock placing, took profits.

Stantronic's first trade was at 110 cents, after it reverse listed into the General Technologies (Gentech) cash shell. This was 12 percent down on the 125 cent closing price of Gentech on Friday following a one for five share consolidation.
Shares, which were listed in the electronics and electrical sector, had dropped even lower to 100 cents by 1020 GMT in volume of almost 618,200 securities -- quiet for a listing.
"It looks like some of the stags who got shares in the private placing are getting out," one dealer said.
Harold Katz, Stantronic's operations director told Reuters the firm was very happy with the listing.
"The skies the limit. We have a very young and dynamic management team...The group is also very acquisition-wise. In the last 10 years we have done 10 acquisitions," he told Reuters.

Sponsoring broker Lowenthal & Co said the private placing had allocated shares at 70 cents. Although there was no public offer, shares in Stantronic could have been acquired through buying stocks in Gentech ahead of the reverse listing.
The other sponsoring broker is Mathison & Hollidge.
Gentech shares last week crept up to 25 cents from 20 cents the week before as players bought into the Stantronic potential.

Stantronic came to the bourse through the acquisition of Stantronic Investments Ltd for 84.5 million rand. Its operations include refridgeration equipment and the supply of electrical and lighting installation for property developments.
Some dealers said that although the share had come off in the morning, it remained a buy up to 115 cents.
Stantronic said in a statement that it expected to grow at a rate of 25 percent this year.

"The creation of the Stantronic group as a listed company has generated the worling capital required for the group to take advantage of future growth opportunities, including those for new acquisitions..," it said.
